resources.string: Lets a bot you paired see this screen and tap, swipe and type for you.

PhoneBridge uses accessibility to read the screen and to perform taps, swipes and typing for the AI bot you paired with this phone. It only works while this service is enabled, only paired bots can send commands, and one bot drives at a time. Turn it off here at any time.
Let your own AI bot use this phone. No central server, end-to-end encrypted.
PhoneBridge needs the accessibility service to see the screen and to tap, swipe and type. Android asks you to switch it on yourself.
Press the test button to check what a bot would see.
Device control is off, so there is nothing to read. Turn on the accessibility service first.
Only bots you pair can send commands. One bot is in control at a time, and you can stop everything from the notification.
Always shows which bot is in control of this phone.
Asks you before a new bot is allowed to control this phone.
This request expired. Ask the bot for a new pairing code.
You can lower the level, never raise it above what the bot asked for. View only reads; Control adds taps, swipes and typing; Full adds shell, settings, apps and moving the relay.
Denied. The bot was not paired.
This request is no longer pending.
Control — plus tap, swipe, type, keys, apps
Full — plus shell, settings, APKs, relay
Show this code to your bot, or send it the link or the .pbpair file. The secret is one-time and dies after ten minutes. Nothing is allowed until you tap Allow on this phone.
The QR code contains the pairing link. The short code works through the relay; the file works when you send it in chat.
This code expired. Generate a new one.
Pair this phone with your bot
Start the bridge first, then pair a bot.
Like Bluetooth devices. Switch one off to close its session, lower its level, or unpair it. Unpairing one bot never touches the others.
No bots paired yet. Pair one from the main screen.
This removes the bot\'s key and closes its session. Other bots keep working.
Every live session is closed and the control queue is cleared. Paired keys stay, so bots can reconnect and ask again.
This only deletes the log on this phone; paired bots stay paired.
The relay forwards encrypted envelopes between this phone and your bots. It can beat here, on your PC, or on a small server you run. Turn it off and remote access stops.
Self-signed relays show a short certificate pin when they start. Paste it here so the phone knows it is talking to your relay.
Start the bridge first to move the heart here.
Three Android permissions make PhoneBridge work. Android asks for each one itself; this screen only takes you there and shows what is still missing.
Lets paired bots read the screen and tap, swipe and type.
Shows the bot in control and asks before a new bot is allowed.
Keeps the encrypted connection alive while the screen is off.

Install APKs, change system settings, run shell commands and read or write files at Full level. These commands need Shizuku, a free open-source app that runs a privileged helper on your phone. Rooted and unrooted phones both work.
Shizuku is already running and PhoneBridge is allowed.
Shizuku has to be started again after every reboot. Open the Shizuku app and start it, then come back here.
Only bots you pair with the Full level can use these commands, and one bot drives at a time. You can revoke the permission in Shizuku at any point.

If Android says this setting is restricted (common for apps not from the Play Store), open App info, tap the three-dot menu at the top right, choose \"Allow restricted settings\", then come back and switch the service on.
PhoneBridge stopped unexpectedly last time. The report below stays on this phone. Copy it and send it to whoever helps you with PhoneBridge.
